verdict.rationale: Buzz's own relay is a WebSocket server that third-party Nostr clients and bot keypairs connect to directly with NIP-29/NIP-42 authentication, and its buzz-acp harness receives @mentions live from that relay, so a gateway-style real-time connection exists. The bot-facing event surface is only lightly documented: the protocol extensions are draft NIPs, there is no machine-readable spec, and the relay API has no deprecation policy. missing for 10: a documented bot-oriented event subscription reference (event kinds, filters, delivery semantics), a stable rather than draft protocol with a versioning/deprecation policy, and independent hands-on corroboration of building a real-time bot against the relay.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a bot that receives messages and events in real time through an events API or gateway connection

citations.quote: Third-party Nostr clients connect directly to `buzz-relay` using NIP-29 and NIP-42 authentication.
buzz-relay # WebSocket relay server — main entry point; also hosts git + huddle audio
The harness listens for @mentions on the relay, prompts your agent, and the agent replies using the Buzz CLI.
